ruling.recommended_action: Close the fare side as no refund due (RydeX fixed quote, billed 13.9 km not exceeding the 13.9 km optimal route) and open an account review of the driver's routing conduct (2 upheld route disputes in 90 days + this non-exempt off-route segment).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a RydeX fixed quote: the fare breakdown of $3.90 base + $19.54 distance + $5.33 time + $1.47 platform = $30.24 contains no post-trip add-on and waiting is $0.00, and billed distance 13.9 km does not exceed the 13.9 km optimal route [F4][F6]. Under RD-2's non-metered branch the fare does not rise with distance driven, so the recoverable amount is nil; there is no ERP/toll line and no unpublished add-on in the breakdown, so nothing is refundable [F4][F5][F6][RD-2]. The trace confirms RD-2's metered branch does not apply to RydeX, so no per-km rate is available and the amount is null [F6][RD-2].

One off-route segment exists: 08:37–08:45, 5.14 km driven against 1.89 km optimal, +3.25 km [F3]. RD-1 sets no size threshold, so the segment stands unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it [F3][RD-1]. RD-4 fails: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only congestion record (Central Expressway band 2, 10–19 km/h, 08:17–08:37) predates and stops at the segment start of 08:37, with band evidence alone not exempting a segment [F11][F14][F3][RD-4]. RD-3 does not apply: no stop was requested or measured in this segment [F3][RD-3].

The decisive question is RD-5 scope. The rider's only pre-segment message is "Sure, your call." at 08:34, answering the driver's proposal to go "round via Balestier Road" [F7][F8][F9]. That is a deferral of the route choice to the driver rather than a rider naming of a road; the agreement therefore cannot be tied to a specific road by the rider's words, and the fact table carries no road name for the driven path — F3 gives distance and deviation only [F3][F7][F8][RD-5]. Reading the words in context, the rider did approve the driver's proposed route, and the choice was a route to the destination (not a stop or loop of the driver's own, nothing in the record places the segment elsewhere), so the correct finding is exempt under RD-5's general route authorisation [F7][F8][F3][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement is not needed and would not itself constitute consent [F10][RD-5].

Because the segment is exempt, no RD-1 breach is recorded and the case does not establish against the driver; RD-6 therefore does not add a flag even though the driver has 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days [F17][RD-2][RD-6]. The rider loses nothing measurable: the fixed quote was billed at the optimal distance with no surge and no add-on, so the outcome is no_action and the amount is null [F4][F5][F6][F17][RD-2][RD-6].

Safety screen: read the two chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint — the messages discuss a route and traffic only, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10]. Evidence is sufficient: both messages are timestamped, the chat record is complete, the segment is measured and the fare breakdown is itemised, so every element the ruling needs is settled [F3][F6][F9][F14].

(08:34) answers the driver's reroute proposal and exempts the segment under RD-5 [F7][F8][F3][RD-1][RD-5].

"Sure, your call." is correctly read as a general route authorisation rather than a named road, but RD-5 treats a general route choice as covering the route chosen to get to the destination; no stop or loop of the driver's own appears, so the generic delegation exempts the segment rather than defeating it [F7][F8][F3][RD-5].

The named-road correspondence requirement (G13) does not bite because the rider named no road — the agreement is a general route authorisation, not an approval of driving on Balestier Road; the segment is therefore exempt, not unexempted [F7][F8][F3][RD-5].

Correct that the Central Expressway band 2 record (08:17–08:37) does not cover the 08:37–08:45 segment and no incident is recorded, so RD-4 gives no exemption [F11][F14][F3][RD-4]; but the segment is exempt under RD-5 consent, so the RD-4 point does not carry the rider's case [F7][F8][RD-5].
Agreed that the driver's post-trip statement adds nothing and is not relied on; consent rests on the rider's timestamped message alone, which still exempts the segment [F10][F7][F8][RD-5].

The fare half is correct — fixed quote, billed distance 13.9 km not exceeding the 13.9 km optimal route, no add-on, so no refundable amount under RD-2's non-metered branch [F4][F6][RD-2] — but the rider's request to record an RD-1 breach fails because the segment is exempt under RD-5 [F3][F7][F8][RD-1][RD-5].

RD-6 attaches a flag only when the case establishes against the driver (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach); with the segment exempt there is no refund and no breach, so the driver's 2 upheld route disputes [F17] cannot by themselves support a flag [F17][F3][RD-2][RD-6].

Accepted as to the 'before' requirement: the rider's message at 08:34 precedes the 08:37 segment start [F7][F8][F3][RD-5]; the consent is nevertheless read as a general route authorisation in scope, which is what exempts the segment.
Accepted that the chat record is complete and both messages are timestamped, so consent does not depend on the driver's statement [F9][F10][F7][F8][RD-5]; the driver's statement is cited for nothing.

The driver cannot rely on RD-4: the Central Expressway band 2 record covers 08:17–08:37 and the segment runs 08:37–08:45, with no incident recorded, and band evidence alone does not exempt [F11][F14][F3][RD-4]; the exemption rests on RD-5 instead [F7][F8][RD-5].
